name: Vespid Dynamics Paralytic Wasp Drone PWD-4 'Yellowjacket'
description: A small quad-rotor drone the size of a fist, painted in Vespid's characteristic yellow-and-black livery, equipped with a retractable syringe containing a paralytic compound. The Yellowjacket autonomously navigates to a designated target, matches their pace, and delivers a single injection — typically to the neck or exposed limb — before returning to its launch point for reload. The paralytic compound immobilizes the target for 15-20 minutes while leaving them fully conscious and aware. The drone's small size and quiet electric motors make it difficult to detect in urban environments, and its yellow-black coloring is both a brand statement and a psychological weapon — in GLMZ, seeing anything yellow and black with rotors means Vespid is watching.
specifications: drone size: 12 cm rotor-to-rotor flight time: 15 minutes operating range: 500 meters from controller syringe payload: 2ml paralytic compound injection method: Retractable spring-loaded syringe paralysis duration: 15-20 minutes motor noise: 35 dB at 2 meters navigation: Autonomous with facial recognition target lock speed: 45 km/h maximum
story_hooks: A string of muggings involve victims being paralyzed by Yellowjacket stings before being robbed — the drones are stolen Vespid units but the paralytic compound is custom-made.
A Yellowjacket loaded with a lethal compound instead of paralytic was deployed in a corporate office — the target died at their desk and the drone returned to its operator before anyone noticed.

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact quadrotor drone with an aggressive insectoid silhouette. The body is distinctly wasp-like — bulbous central thorax with four articulated arm-mounted rotors splayed outward. A menacing retractable syringe protrudes from the ventral surface like a stinger. The yellow-and-black striping creates immediate visual threat recognition, mimicking natural predator coloration.
physical_description.dimensions: 12 cm rotor-to-rotor (diagonal span). Central body sphere approximately 4 cm in diameter. Retractable syringe extends 3 cm when deployed. Total mass roughly 280-320 grams.
physical_description.weight_description: Lightweight and nimble in hand — feels almost delicate until you realize what it carries. Balanced distribution across four rotors makes it sit naturally in an open palm. The syringe payload adds subtle forward weight bias.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade polymer frame with carbon-fiber rotor arms. Alloy motor housings. Glass-reinforced polymer body shell. Spring-loaded syringe housing in surgical stainless steel.
physical_description.finish: High-gloss enamel on primary body panels — characteristic Vespid yellow with jet-black racing stripes. Rotor arms finished in matte black anodized aluminum. Motor housings show brushed metallic silver. The syringe delivery mechanism has a cold surgical sheen — polished stainless with micro-etched measurement markings.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: Safety yellow (pantone 116C) with gloss finish. Secondary: Jet black stripes running along the body seams and rotor arms. Accents: Silver motor housings and stainless-steel syringe. Small red LED indicator behind transparent panel on dorsal surface.
physical_description.grip_texture: Smooth polymer body with subtle grip ridges molded into the sides. Rotor arms have light texture to prevent slipping during transport. The syringe trigger mechanism has rubberized coating for positive tactile feedback.
distinctive_features: Four articulated rotor arms that fold inward for compact storage
Retractable spring-loaded syringe with visible paralytic compound (amber/clear fluid in transparent housing)
Micro-perforated ventilation grilles on sides for motor cooling
Embedded facial-recognition camera lens (small dark circle, dorsal surface, center)
Vespid Dynamics logo — stylized wasp silhouette — laser-etched on rotor motor housings
Faint wear patterns around syringe housing from repeated deployment cycles
Tiny alignment grooves on body for rapid mounting into launch dock
Microscopic serial number etched into syringe base (Vespid tracking)
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Vespid Dynamics hexagonal logo stamped in black on yellow dorsal panel. Model designation 'PWD-4' printed in small Arial font below logo. Serial number laser-etched on syringe housing and on underside of main body. Tiny copyright notice on motor housing in microscopic print.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field units show light operational wear — minor scuffs on rotor blade tips, slight dulling of yellow enamel at contact points, microscopic polymer stress marks around syringe deployment mechanism. Well-maintained units have polished syringes and pristine rotor blades. Heavily-used units show visible yellow paint chipping and replacement rotor arms in OEM packaging.
